---
title: "Go: net/http, chi, Echo, and Gin"
description: "Add passwordless auth (passkeys, magic links, email and SMS codes) to a Go net/http, chi, Echo, or Gin app without writing JWT code, with the official seamless-auth-go adapter: install, a complete app, configuration, and cookie and bearer transport."
sidebar:
  order: 3.2
---

`github.com/fells-code/seamless-auth-go` is the official Seamless Auth server adapter for Go. It is
a plain `net/http` handler and middleware, so it works with the standard library mux, chi, Echo,
and Gin. It mounts the `/auth` routes the frontend SDKs call, holds the session in signed
`HttpOnly` cookies on your own domain, and gives you `RequireAuth` for your own routes. You do not
write token parsing, JWKS fetching, cookie signing, or refresh logic, and the module has no
dependencies outside the Go standard library.

Use it when your backend is Go and you want passkeys, magic links, email or SMS codes, or OAuth
sign-in against a Seamless Auth server (self-hosted `seamless-auth-api` or a managed instance). It
is held to the same conformance suite as the Express, Fastify, Python, and Rust adapters. For other
languages see [Server SDKs And Adapters](/build/server-sdks).

Source: [fells-code/seamless-auth-go](https://github.com/fells-code/seamless-auth-go). Current
release: `v0.2.0` (pre-1.0, so the public API may change between minor versions).

---

## Install

```bash
go get github.com/fells-code/seamless-auth-go@v0.2.0
```

It needs Go 1.22 or later. The package name is `seamlessauth`.

---

## A Complete App

This mounts the auth routes at `/auth`, protects `/api/me`, and reads the current user. It follows
the reference app the conformance suite drives (`conformance/refapp/main.go`).

```go
package main

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"log"
	"net/http"
	"os"

	seamlessauth "github.com/fells-code/seamless-auth-go"
)

func main() {
	auth, err := seamlessauth.New(seamlessauth.Options{
		AuthServerURL:    os.Getenv("AUTH_SERVER_URL"),
		AuthServerIssuer: os.Getenv("AUTH_SERVER_ISSUER"), // empty means AuthServerURL
		CookieSecret:     os.Getenv("COOKIE_SIGNING_KEY"), // 32 characters or more
		ServiceSecret:    os.Getenv("API_SERVICE_TOKEN"),  // the auth API's API_SERVICE_TOKEN
		JWKSKid:          os.Getenv("JWKS_KID"),
	})
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}

	mux := http.NewServeMux()

	// The auth routes, at /auth, which is where the frontend SDKs call.
	mux.Handle("/auth/", http.StripPrefix("/auth", auth.Handler()))

	// Your own route, behind the adapter's guard. RequireAuth answers 401 without a session.
	mux.Handle("GET /api/me", auth.RequireAuth(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		user, _ := seamlessauth.UserFromContext(r.Context())
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
		json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(map[string]any{"id": user.ID, "roles": user.Roles})
	})))

	log.Fatal(http.ListenAndServe(":"+os.Getenv("PORT"), mux))
}
```

- `seamlessauth.New(Options)` returns an `*Adapter`, or an error on a missing auth server URL or a secret shorter
  than 32 characters, so a misconfigured app fails to boot.
- `auth.Handler()` serves every auth route. Mount it under `/auth` with `http.StripPrefix`.
- `auth.RequireAuth(next)` answers 401 unless the request carries a session, and puts a `*User`
  on the request context. `seamlessauth.UserFromContext(ctx)` reads it.
- `User` has `ID`, `Roles`, `Email`, `Phone`, and `Token` (the auth API access token). On a bearer
  request `Email` and `Phone` are empty, because the access token does not carry them.

There is no role middleware in the module. Check `user.Roles` in your handler or in middleware of
your own placed after `RequireAuth`.

For a web app on another origin, wrap the mux in credentialed CORS for that origin (the standard
library has none; use the CORS middleware of your router or a package such as `rs/cors`).

### chi, Echo, And Gin

The handler and middleware are plain `net/http`, so each router wraps them:

```go
// chi
r.Mount("/auth", http.StripPrefix("/auth", auth.Handler()))
r.With(auth.RequireAuth).Get("/api/me", me)

// Echo
e.Any("/auth/*", echo.WrapHandler(http.StripPrefix("/auth", auth.Handler())))
e.GET("/api/me", echo.WrapHandler(auth.RequireAuth(http.HandlerFunc(me))))

// Gin
g.Any("/auth/*path", gin.WrapH(http.StripPrefix("/auth", auth.Handler())))
g.GET("/api/me", gin.WrapH(auth.RequireAuth(http.HandlerFunc(me))))
```

Here `me` is an `http.HandlerFunc` like the one above. In every case your handler reads the user
with `seamlessauth.UserFromContext(r.Context())`.

## Configuration

The adapter reads no environment variables itself. The names below are the ones the Seamless
starters, the conformance reference app, and `seamless init` use, so a project the CLI wrote
already has them in `.env`.

| Variable             | Option             | Value                                                                                                              |
| -------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `AUTH_SERVER_URL`    | `AuthServerURL`    | Where your server reaches the auth API, for example `http://localhost:5312`, or the Auth Server URL from the portal |
| `AUTH_SERVER_ISSUER` | `AuthServerIssuer` | Only when the auth API signs as a different URL (the `seamless init --local` Docker stack signs as `http://auth:5312`) |
| `COOKIE_SIGNING_KEY` | `CookieSecret`     | Any secret of 32 characters or more, for example `openssl rand -base64 48`                                          |
| `API_SERVICE_TOKEN`  | `ServiceSecret`    | The auth API's `API_SERVICE_TOKEN` (self-hosted), or a service token generated in the portal (managed)              |
| `JWKS_KID`           | `JWKSKid`          | `kid` header on the service tokens the adapter signs, not the auth API's signing key id; `dev-main` on a local stack |

`Options` also has:

| Option                                        | Default                                  | Purpose                                                                                  |
| --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Audience`                                    | `AuthServerIssuer`                       | Expected `aud` of the auth API's tokens                                                  |
| `CookieDomain`                                | none                                     | Cookie `Domain`                                                                          |
| `InsecureCookies`                             | `false`                                  | Drops `Secure`, for local development over plain HTTP on a host other than `localhost`  |
| `CookieSameSite`                              | `None`, or `Lax` with `InsecureCookies`  | Cookie `SameSite`                                                                        |
| `AllowedOrigins`                              | none                                     | The only cross-origin callers allowed to change state while cookies are `SameSite=None` |
| `AccessCookieName`, `RefreshCookieName`       | `seamless-access`, `seamless-refresh`    | Session cookie names                                                                     |
| `RegistrationCookieName`, `PreAuthCookieName` | `seamless-ephemeral`                     | Sign-in flow cookie names                                                                |
| `Deliver`                                     | none                                     | Send OTP codes and magic links through your own transports                               |
| `ResolveClientIP`                             | the connecting peer                      | The end user's address; use `seamlessauth.TrustedProxies("10.0.0.0/8")` behind a proxy   |
| `DisableManifestFetch`                        | `false`                                  | Use only the manifest embedded in this version                                           |
| `HTTPClient`, `Logf`                          | defaults                                 | Outbound client and logger                                                               |

### Delivering codes yourself

Without `Deliver`, the auth API sends OTP codes and magic links. With it, the adapter asks the API
for the message and hands it to you as a `Delivery` (`Kind`, `To`, `Token`, `MagicLinkURL`,
`SignInURL`). A returned error answers 502 `delivery_failed`.

```go
Deliver: func(ctx context.Context, d seamlessauth.Delivery) error {
	return mailer.Send(ctx, d.To, d.Kind, d.Token, d.MagicLinkURL)
},
```

### Serving the admin console

`auth.ConsoleHandler()` serves the Seamless admin dashboard from your API, proxied from the auth
API:

```go
mux.Handle("/console/", http.StripPrefix("/console", auth.ConsoleHandler()))
```

Add your API's origin to the auth server's `ORIGINS` so passkey ceremonies started in the console
verify.

---

## Cookie And Bearer Transport

The same `/auth` routes serve two contracts:

- **Browsers** get cookies. The adapter keeps the auth API's tokens in signed `HttpOnly` cookies
  and refreshes the session silently on the auth routes. Page scripts never see a token.
- **Native clients** (mobile apps, CLIs) send `x-seamless-auth-transport: bearer`. Session-issuing
  responses then return `token` and `refreshToken` in the body and set no cookie, and the client
  refreshes with `POST /auth/refresh` and `Authorization: Bearer <refreshToken>`.

`RequireAuth` accepts either the session cookie or an auth API access token in
`Authorization: Bearer`, and the cookie wins when both are present. It reads the `Cookie` header
itself, so it works on any route, and it does not refresh. `auth.Authenticate(r)` runs the same
check without answering the request (and without the cross-site check below).

While cookies are `SameSite=None`, a state-changing request `RequireAuth` admits on the cookie from
another site (`Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`, or an `Origin` outside `AllowedOrigins`) answers 403
`cross_site_request_blocked`. The auth routes only accept JSON request bodies (`application/json`
or a `+json` type); anything else answers 415 `unsupported_media_type`. The frontend SDKs already
send JSON.

See [Bearer Transport For Native Clients](/build/server-sdks#bearer-transport-for-native-clients)
for the full contract, which every adapter shares.

---

## How The Frontend Talks To It

Every frontend SDK calls `${apiHost}/auth/...`, so point it at this server's origin, for example
`<AuthProvider apiHost="http://localhost:3000">` in [React](/build/react-sdk). The same `apiHost`
option exists in [Angular](/build/angular-sdk), [Vue](/build/vue-sdk), [Svelte](/build/svelte-sdk),
and [React Native](/build/react-native-sdk). Browser requests to your own protected routes need
`credentials: 'include'` when the web app runs on another origin.

---

## Version Compatibility

| `seamless-auth-go` | Auth API         | Go    |
| ------------------ | ---------------- | ----- |
| v0.2.0             | v0.18.0 or later | 1.22+ |

Which routes the adapter serves comes from the adapter manifest the auth API publishes at
`/.well-known/seamless-adapter.json`, first served by auth API v0.18.0, so a new API route works
without a new module release. The adapter fetches it on the first request and keeps it for the life
of the process. If the API serves none, it falls back to the copy embedded in the module. Run auth
API v0.18.0 or later: the adapter sends the OTP and magic-link send routes as `POST`, which v0.17.0
answers with 404. `seamless-cli` 0.22.0 and later scaffold v0.18.0. In a project generated by an
older CLI, bump the `ghcr.io/fells-code/seamless-auth-api` image tag to `v0.18.0`.

---

## Conformance

The adapter is held to the adapter conformance suite in `seamless-cli`
([`verify/CONFORMANCE.md`](https://github.com/fells-code/seamless-cli/blob/main/verify/CONFORMANCE.md)),
the same suite the Express and Fastify adapters pass, in CI on every change. To run it yourself you
need Docker, a checkout of `seamless-auth-api`, and the `seamless` CLI:

```bash
PORT=8080 AUTH_SERVER_URL=http://localhost:5312 AUTH_SERVER_ISSUER=http://auth-api:5312 \
  API_SERVICE_TOKEN=verify-dev-service-token-not-a-real-secret \
  COOKIE_SIGNING_KEY=verify-dev-service-token-not-a-real-secret JWKS_KID=dev-main \
  go run ./conformance/refapp &

SEAMLESS_API_DIR=../seamless-auth-api seamless verify --adapter-url=http://localhost:8080
```

---

## Starter Template

`seamless-templates` has a Gin api starter (`templates/api/gin`, status beta) built on this
adapter, which `seamless init` selects with `--gin` or `--api=gin`. It ships in templates `v0.18.0`,
which `seamless-cli` 0.22.0 and later scaffold together with auth API v0.18.0:

```bash
npx seamless-cli init my-app --local --yes --email=you@example.com --gin
```

---

## Do Not Write Your Own Token Verification

Use `RequireAuth` or `Authenticate` rather than decoding the session cookie or the access token
yourself. They check the cookie signature, the auth API's JWKS signature, issuer, audience, expiry,
and token type, and `RequireAuth` adds the cross-site rules above. A hand-rolled JWT check usually
misses one of those, and the cookie format is internal to the adapter.
